==Problem==
The Fort Worth Zoo has a number of two-legged birds and a number of four-legged mammals. On one visit to the zoo, Margie counted 200 heads and 522 legs. How many of the animals that Margie counted were two-legged birds?

<imath> \textbf{(A)}\hspace{.05in}61\qquad\textbf{(B)}\hspace{.05in}122\qquad\textbf{(C)}\hspace{.05in}139\qquad\textbf{(D)}\hspace{.05in}150\qquad\textbf{(E)}\hspace{.05in}161 </imath>

==Solution 1: Algebra==
Let the number of two-legged birds be <imath>x</imath> and the number of four-legged mammals be <imath>y</imath>. We can now use systems of equations to solve this problem.

Write two equations:

<imath> 2x + 4y = 522 </imath>

<imath> x + y = 200 </imath>

Now multiply the latter equation by <imath> 2 </imath>.

<imath> 2x + 4y = 522 </imath>

<imath> 2x + 2y = 400 </imath>

By subtracting the second equation from the first equation, we find that <imath> 2y = 122 \implies y = 61 </imath>. Since there were <imath> 200 </imath> heads, meaning that there were <imath> 200 </imath> animals, there were <imath> 200 - 61 =  \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 139} </imath> two-legged birds.

==Solution 2: Cheating the System==
First, we "assume" there are <imath>200</imath> two-legged birds only, and <imath>0</imath> four-legged mammals. Of course, this poses a problem, as then there would only be <imath>200\cdot2=400</imath> legs.

Now we have to do some swapping--for every two-legged bird we swap for a four-legged mammal, we gain <imath>2</imath> legs. For example, if we swapped one bird for one mammal, giving <imath>199</imath> birds and <imath>1</imath> mammal, there would be <imath>400 + 1(2) = 402</imath> legs. If we swapped two birds for two mammals, there would be <imath>400 + 2(2) = 404</imath> legs. If we swapped <imath>50</imath> birds for <imath>50</imath> mammals, there would be <imath>400 + 50(2) = 500</imath> legs.

==Solution 3: Add two legs for each bird==
Let's add <imath>2</imath> legs for each bird and assume each bird has four-legged as each mammal. So the total legs of these birds and mammals would be <imath>4*200=800</imath>. Actually, there were only <imath>522</imath> legs. The difference between these two numbers exactly gives us the number of all the legs we added for all birds: <imath>800 - 522 = 278</imath>. Because each bird was added by 2 legs, so the total number of birds would be <imath> 278/2 = \boxed{\textbf{(C)}\ 139} </imath> two-legged birds. ---LarryFlora
